title: Staff sprint ceremony and priority realignment
summary: Quarter-end all-hands focused on sprint outcomes, short-term priorities, regional capacity planning, and a brief risk/readiness check for upcoming Dedicated customer pilots. Leadership emphasized reliability levers and asked teams to own a reduced set of deliverables for the next six weeks.
topics: Priority realignment for next six weeks
Regional capacity and spot market hedging
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-10 17:00 UTC | Duration: ~75 minutes | Location: All-hands video call
Attendees: Maya Chen (CEO), Diego Alvarez (VP Product), Lena Park (Head Eng), Omar Sheikh (Head Ops), Priya Rao (Head Sales), Hannah Liu (Head People), plus entire staff channel

[00:00] Maya: ok hi everyone, thanks for joining on a Thursday afternoon. i'm gonna kick things off, i'm Maya, quick agenda — sprint recap, priorities, region/capacity readout, security quick note, then q and a. try to keep it tight.
[00:18] Crowd noise / applause (indistinct)
[00:22] Diego: quick scoreboard — shipped the runtime batching story, improved tail latency by our metrics, and the optimize toolkit hit the new suggestion engine. big thumbs up to eng and infra. there are still some regressions in mem caching though, so we need follow ups.
[00:38] Lena: yeah, just to call out — the continuous batching change reduced 95th by about 18% on our p99 tests, but we saw a small throughput dip on 2 long-seq models under heavy KV caching. possibility it's an interaction with the new kernel selector.
[00:58] Maya: okay, so tradeoffs. we shipped latency wins but it cost a bit on throughput in certain tails. the ask for the next cycle is to prioritize predictable SLOs for the top 3 production routes. keep optimizations, but no regression on published SLOs.
[01:18] Speaker 4 (Jeremy?): question — will that impact the Dedicated customers?
[01:22] Omar: short answer, yes some. we're flagging affected model types and will push auto-routing to fall back to the stable kernel for those routes. that fallback will be conservative and opt-in for Dedicated tenants until we validate in canary.
[01:40] Diego: and to be clear — fallback means a small cost delta, maybe 2–4% more token cost on those flows, but keeps latency tight. sales and CS, we'll have a note for customers.
[01:58] Priya: i'll coordinate the customer comms. for anyone on renewals, flagging this now so we're not surprised.
[02:10] Hannah: small HR note — we hired 6 people this quarter, good ramp, please update your onboarding buddies list. also, holiday OOO window reminders.
[02:30] [02:30] Maya: now the realignment — we're asking each squad to cut non-critical scope and focus on three measurable outcomes for the next six weeks: 1) SLO improvement for high-value routes, 2) Dedicated pilot checklist completed, 3) hiring or documentation to reduce tribal knowledge. that's it.
[02:58] Lena: to operationalize that — eng will publish a sprint-lite board tomorrow with the top 3 outcomes per squad. also we'll freeze new large infra changes that touch kernel selection until we complete the canary.
[03:18] [03:18] Ravi (Field Eng): quick note about regions — two pilot customers in APAC requested private deployments in January. do we have capacity?
[03:28] Omar: capacity readout — short answer: able but tight. our US-hosted pool has headroom; EMEA is fine; APAC we need to reserve a few Dedicated units or leverage partner regions. we're working with cloud partners for burst nodes.
[03:45] Diego: caveat — some of that headroom depends on our spot/ondemand mix and quantization profiles. if teams can tighten quantization to q4-ish profiles (laughs) we can get more throughput.
[04:00] [04:00] Maya: stop there — i want a concrete plan. ops: produce a 30/60/90 capacity plan for APAC with a risk column. engineering: give a list of the top model families that need special kernel treatment. sales: prioritize pilots that are time-boxed for Jan/Feb.
[04:18] Omar: will do — output on Friday.
[04:20] [04:20] Diego: another item — we ran two internal perf benchmarks last week, one on the latest quantized llama variant and one on a long-context transformer. results were noisy; instrumentation needs calibration. note: some telemetry labels got dropped, looks like a festival of label mismatches.
[04:40] Speaker (Tom - Security): security quick note — SOC2 re-audit prep is on schedule, but a few docs are stale: key rotation logs, KMS config detail, and we need fresh third-party risk assessments from our pod vendors. also reminder: SSO onboarding must use SCIM where possible.
[04:58] Maya: thanks tom. any blockers from legal/compliance?
[05:02] Tom: nothing critical but the audit team wants clearer retention policies for debug logs tied to customer requests; we'll share a template.
[05:12] [05:12] Audience murmur / brief Qs in chat
[05:18] Maya: ok open q&a — please be concise.
[05:22] Speaker 6 (Allie - Eng): the canary plan — do we pin canaries to a single DC or multi-dc? we saw cross-region flaps before.
[05:30] Lena: prefer single DC for initial canary to isolate infra variance. then expand to multi-dc for latency and routing validation. also, we need a rollback playbook that includes automatic KV cache flush so we don't serve stale prefixes.
[05:50] Maya: good. who's owning the rollback playbook?
[05:54] Lena: ops and platform — Omar and Jeremy will co-own.
[05:58] Omar: noted. will publish runbook Wednesday.
[06:02] [06:02] Priya: commercial note — we're seeing more RFPs that ask for private deployments + audit logs + per-route latency SLO. we should consider packaging a "pilot pack" that includes these items and a short bench report.
[06:18] Diego: yes, product marketing and sales, we should make a one-pager. Priya, can you lead?
[06:22] Priya: yes — i'll share draft next week.
[06:26] [06:26] Maya: two quick culture org changes — first, we're creating a small "ops safety" working group to reduce incident toil; second, a cross-functional "pilot success" pod to make sure Dedicated pilots hit customer SLOs. details to follow.
[06:44] Hannah: quick people update — comp cycles are later this quarter, managers please complete calibration form by Dec 20th. also, we will pilot a flexible holiday schedule for region X, more on that by Friday.
[06:58] [06:58] Audience question: Q: any change to oncall?
[07:02] Maya: no major change now. we will do a review.
[07:06] [07:06] Diego: competitive note — Anthropic and OpenAI have some new pricing moves, and big cloud providers are bundling hosted endpoints with managed infra. we need to keep evangelizing our production economics story.
[07:24] Priya: add a one-pager for sales about cost tradeoffs: dedicated vs hosted vs private, with typical % cost deltas and latency expectations.
[07:34] Maya: all right, wrap up — quick recap of asks and owners.
[07:38] [07:38] Diego: Outcome owners: eng—SLOs for top routes (Lena); ops—APAC capacity plan 30/60/90 (Omar); sales—pilot pack + one-pager (Priya); security—audit doc updates (Tom); HR—onboarding & comp timelines (Hannah).
[07:54] Lena: and engineering will freeze large kernel changes until canary validates, but smaller infra bugfixes ok.
[08:02] Maya: last thing — gratitude for shipping hard this quarter, but also remember to pace, safety first. we'll follow up with written summary. thank you.
[08:18] [08:18] END
